messages.subject: Re: Session time for download
messages.subject_clean: Session time for download
messages.body_plain:
Scott: an easy workaround would be to have two buttons, one for "generate the data" and one for "download the data".  Have the "download" button disabled to begin with, when you click on "generate" it'll do all the computation, when it's done it'll enable the "download" button, and clicking on "download" will simply serve the file that was already created before

On Thursday, 18 February 2016 12:12:07 UTC-8, Scott Kravitz wrote:
> Is there any way to extend the timeout of downloadHandler? I have a large amount of computations that takes about 2 minutes, and I haven't been able to find a way to speed up the code. I consistently get a "
> No data received
>
> ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE" error. Is there any way that I can get around this?
>
> Thanks!
> Scott
>
> On Friday, November 7, 2014 at 2:52:08 AM UTC-5, Tiph Martin wrote:
> >
> > Hi Cheng,
> >
> > I am going to look at about hard-coded timeout in Shiny Server
> >
> > Currently, I am using reactive expression to create the plot in png format and after, I give the possibility to download it. But I need to rerun the function "cometplotPrint()" to produce the pdf, png or eps files.
> >
> > I tried to create a pdf or png or eps using reactive expression but I didn't find the way to visualise a pdf or eps files in-app plot and to link on file to download without running the function "cometplotPrint()".
> > So if you have example shiny apps to do that, I am very happy to follow it.
> >
> > Unfortunately, the calculation is done during the plot because it creates annotation tracks (connexion to biological databases : ENSEMBL mart and UCSC).
> >
> > Tiph

messages.subject: Re: If is possible Interactive UI using sliderInput( ) that will be appear whith the user want?
messages.subject_clean: If is possible Interactive UI using sliderInput( ) that will be appear whith the user want?
messages.body_plain:
I don't have a solution because I don't exactly understand the problem, but please note that the solutions given here would not work from the simple reason that every input must have a unique ID.  This is not just a good practice, it's something that MUST be followed, otherwise your app will not work properly.  The first argument to `sliderInput()` is an ID, and that has to be different for every single input

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

1.) I'am writing a MediaWiki extension which embeds Shiny app code into MediaWiki. The wiki copies the app code into the shiny-server app directory which is outside the Apache document root. Since the MediaWiki is run by the Apache user, I created a subdir in the shiny-server app directory which can be accessed by the Apache user. Could the app.R files be accessed somehow?

2.) For an specific app I have confidential data. If I put them in a data directory of the app can the data files itself accessed (except from the app)?

Thanks in advance

Sigbert

messages.subject: Re: SVGAnnotation Package Error when deploying shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: SVGAnnotation Package Error when deploying shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Well thats very sad.  It looks like the DESCRIPTION file in that repository is incorrect.

Ultimately the problem here is that the package hosted on Bioconductor does not contain the Repository or BiocViews field in its DESCRIPTION so its impossible to detect the origin of the package. We had a workaround in place at one time, but it got removed since it was a bit of a hack. We can look into doing something similar again.

However if I were you, I would look into replacing the SVGAnnotation package with something else if at all possible, it doesn't seem to be maintained any more, and it's prone to breakage because of the DESCRIPTION file issue.

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
I'm sorry, I don't have the time to go into specifics and solve this problem. To reiterate: every single input must have a different, unique inputId parameter.  In the first code you provided, all the inputs had the id "a", which means you would not be able to retrieve the values of all the different inputs.  In the code you just provided, the inputId is given by `B[i]`, but the B vector only has 3 elements, so if you try to change the num input to any number larger than 3, you should get an error.

The idea is:

 HTML('<input id="warnMsg" type="text" style="display:none;" value="" class="shiny-bound-input" onchange="genWarnMsg()">'))

function genWarnMsg() {

messages.subject: Re: Geolocate User Location in R Leaflet
messages.subject_clean: Geolocate User Location in R Leaflet
messages.body_plain:
The JavaScript API is this:

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Geolocation/watchPosition

So you could include a .js file (using includeScript(), for example) with the following:

navigator.geolocation.watchPosition(function(pos) {
  Shiny.onInputChange("userPosition", {
    latitude: pos.coords.latitude,
    longitude: pos.coords.longitude,
    altitude: pos.coords.altitude,
    accuracy: pos.coords.accuracy // in meters
    altitudeAccuracy: pos.coords.altitudeAccuracy // in meters,
    heading: pos.coords.heading,
    speed: pos.coords.speed
  });
}, null, {enableHighAccuracy: true});

That would let you observe input$userPosition from the server, and it should update whenever the position changes. You can then use leafletProxy to recenter the map on the new location, and/or move a marker, or whatever.

messages.subject: Re: suppress red error messages in shiny webpage
messages.subject_clean: suppress red error messages in shiny webpage
messages.body_plain:
It is possible now by inserting this snippet into the top of either app.R, or if you have a ui.R/server.R style app, at the top of global.R (make one in the app dir if you don't have one already):

options(shiny.error = function() {
  stop("An error has occurred")
})

This has the drawback that it will fully swallow your errors, your log file will contain only nonsense like this:

Warning: Error in handle: An error has occurred
No stack trace available
Error in handle() : An error has occurred
Warning: Error in handle: An error has occurred
No stack trace available

So clearly you don't want to use this during development. You could do something like this:

if (!interactive()) {
  options(shiny.error = function() {
    stop("An error has occurred")
  })
}

which would probably work for most cases.

I think we can do better than this though; ideally there'd be an option in Shiny Server, Shiny Server Pro, and ShinyApps.io that let you specify that you want errors hidden from the client but still logged on the server side.

Anyway, I've filed an issue to track this further work:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1123

In the meantime, please let me know if the workaround I've proposed is enough to get you unblocked. Thanks.

messages.subject: `leafletProxy` has stopped working
messages.subject_clean: `leafletProxy` has stopped working
messages.body_plain:
I just updated a bunch of packages and now it seems that `shiny::leafletProxy` has stopped working.

I wasn't sure if this was the case at first, but my suspicion was confirmed when I ran the example code provided in the 'Using Leaflet With Shiny'  <https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/shiny.html>tutorial and got the following:

library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(RColorBrewer)

ui <- bootstrapPage(
  tags$style(type = "text/css", "html, body {width:100%;height:100%}"),
  leafletOutput("map", width = "100%", height = "100%"),
  absolutePanel(top = 10, right = 10,
    sliderInput("range", "Magnitudes", min(quakes$mag), max(quakes$mag),
      value = range(quakes$mag), step = 0.1
    ),
    selectInput("colors", "Color Scheme",
      rownames(subset(brewer.pal.info, category %in% c("seq", "div")))
    ),
    checkboxInput("legend", "Show legend", TRUE)
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # Reactive expression for the data subsetted to what the user selected
  filteredData <- reactive({
    quakes[quakes$mag >= input$range[1] & quakes$mag <= input$range[2],]
  })

  # This reactive expression represents the palette function,
  # which changes as the user makes selections in UI.
  colorpal <- reactive({
    colorNumeric(input$colors, quakes$mag)
  })

  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    # Use leaflet() here, and only include aspects of the map that
    # won't need to change dynamically (at least, not unless the
    # entire map is being torn down and recreated).
    leaflet(quakes) %>% addTiles() %>%
      fitBounds(~min(long), ~min(lat), ~max(long), ~max(lat))
  })

  # Incremental changes to the map (in this case, replacing the
  # circles when a new color is chosen) should be performed in
  # an observer. Each independent set of things that can change
  # should be managed in its own observer.
  observe({
    pal <- colorpal()

    leafletProxy("map", data = filteredData()) %>%
      clearShapes() %>%
      addCircles(radius = ~10^mag/10, weight = 1, color = "#777777",
        fillColor = ~pal(mag), fillOpacity = 0.7, popup = ~paste(mag)
      )
  })

  # Use a separate observer to recreate the legend as needed.
  observe({
    proxy <- leafletProxy("map", data = quakes)

    # Remove any existing legend, and only if the legend is
    # enabled, create a new one.
    proxy %>% clearControls()
    if (input$legend) {
      pal <- colorpal()
      proxy %>% addLegend(position = "bottomright",
        pal = pal, values = ~mag
      )
    }
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

## app.R ##
library(shiny)

library(leaflet)

# UI: Header ----
header <- dashboardHeader(
        title = "Title"
)
# UI: Siderbar ----
sidebar <- dashboardSidebar(
        sidebarMenu(id="tabs",
                    menuItem("About", tabName = "about", icon = icon("question"),selected=TRUE)

        )
)
# UI: Body ----
body <- dashboardBody(
        fillPage(padding = 10,
                tags$style(type = "text/css",
                           ".third-fill { width: 33%; height: 100%; }",

messages.subject: Re: issue with shiny progress indicator
messages.subject_clean: issue with shiny progress indicator
messages.body_plain:
Your first code makes no sense. The TraitsModel call is the "expr" argument to withProgress, the function that will be evaluated and is expected to contain calls to incProgress or setProgress. It presumably doesn't, so that's why your bar isn't working very well. The for (i in 1:20) code seems to be being passed to withProgress as the session argument, which might cause weird behaviour.

In your second example, it should be no surprise that the bar completes before your function is called, because that's exactly what you've told it to do. You set the message and detail, then your for loop runs and increments the bar to max, then TraitsModel is called. You need to do this some other way.

The fundamental problem with this approach is that you're relying on Sys.sleep though. This approach makes no sense because you have no idea how long TraitsModel will take. Maybe your machine will get a hardware upgrade and the code will suddenly be much faster, or maybe there will be heavy load when the user happens to run the function and it takes much longer than expected. A simple time-based progress bar doesn't make much sense in this context. If there aren't obvious points inside TraitsModel where you could increment the bar, it might be better to just use a spinner so that the user understands that something is happening, but that they still have to wait.

Hi all,

Our department also discovered Shiny, so we're using it more and more as an interface to packages we develop here. Many upsides, but we experience a very serious downside as well:

The packages we develop, contain a whole set of checks and informative error messages to catch every mistake a silly user can make. But when creating an interface to these packages, all those checks become useless:

- the errors aren't conveniently displayed in the app.
- more seriously, errors just stop the app from running when deployed over the server and accessed through a web browser.

I am familiar with need() and validate(), but reimplementing all checks we have in the package in the app seems like a lot of redundant work. Right now we succeed by wrapping everything in tryCatch(), and using this to catch a possible error message for redirection to a verbatim display. This works, but it still feels bulky and unnecessary complicated.

Is there a way to graciously redirect stderr to any kind of output, and prevent the app from stopping with every error it occurs?

Thank you in advance.
Cheers
Joris

messages.subject: Re: R/Shiny vs FileMaker (discussion about data visualization and reporting)
messages.subject_clean: R/Shiny vs FileMaker (discussion about data visualization and reporting)
messages.body_plain:
I have not used FileMaker Pro in over twenty years so it's not really fair for me to draw comparisons. In fact I'd be very surprised if the overlap between FileMaker Pro users and R users is very large at all, as (correct me if I'm wrong) FileMaker Pro is primarily aimed at businesspeople at small businesses or small workgroups within larger businesses, while R is aimed squarely at statisticians and data scientists.
Because R and Shiny are primarily code- and text-file based (rather than a binary file format like FileMaker):
Scripts and apps are reproducible, can be version controlled, and can easily be reviewed by others. For me, this alone would make me shy away from FileMaker for anything that's important to get right; the idea of building apps without version control is frankly terrifying to me. It's not just about backups (which you can obviously do with FM or anything else that uses files), it's about knowing what changed when, and being able to review what you've changed before you make a commit.
You can easily set up test and staging environments to review your apps on non-live data before committing changes to production.
You can have two people working independently on the same app's code, without disturbing each other, yet their changes can easily be merged together (automatically or manually) whenever each is ready to commit those changes. (i.e. git branch)
You have to know how to code. You have done some R so you know it takes patience (and talent, to some degree) to learn how to program proficiently. This is too high a barrier of entry for tons of people out there, especially if their databases/apps are not important enough to them to make a big time investment.
R and Shiny are designed for modularity and re-use (at the function, script, and package levels). This means it's very easy to leverage solutions that others in the community have come across, and this particular community has an extremely deep-rooted culture of sharing. (See the many thousands of packages available on CRAN, BioConductor, R-Forge, and GitHub, compared to the few dozen FileMaker Pro modules on modulefilemaker.org <http://modulefilemaker.org>.)
Innovation in R is primarily driven by the community, not by the small group of people in R-Core. I imagine that as a FileMaker user, if there are new features you want to see in FileMaker, you generally have to wait for the company's engineers to implement them.
I don't know enough about FileMaker to provide a detailed breakdown of the kinds of charts you can make in R vs. FM, but I would be stunned if FM was even close to as flexible as R's base graphics, ggplot2, and/or lattice. A google image search of "R graphics" should give you an eyeful. In particular, ggplot2 strikes a really appealing balance, being high-level enough to be very pleasant to use but low-level enough that the universe of chart types you can make with it is enormous. And there are newer packages like rbokeh, plotly, and ggvis that let you work with similar grammars but give you interactive visualizations instead of static ones.
I really don't know anything about statistical modeling, forecasting, diagnostics, etc. but I'm told R is really good at them. :)
R can work with many common databases and file formats but I'd check to make sure it can work with FileMaker. If not, I imagine you'll be doing a lot of importing and exporting using CSVs and that doesn't sound like fun.
There's a lot LOT more than R can do that I haven't gone into, but hopefully that provides a start.

messages.subject: Pre-Load progress bar/spinner - as app starts
messages.subject_clean: Pre-Load progress bar/spinner - as app starts
messages.body_plain:
Hi there -

After searching a bit, I'm a little lost.
I've got a shiny app that needs to pull data from a database across the interwebs.
No big deal, as RMySQL works like a charm.  The problem is the traffic delay.  It can take 15-60 seconds to load up.  I only need to load data at startup, doesn't need to be responsive at all.

However, the users can think things are broken & click elsewhere.

I need a progress bar or a spinner to show up - but only as the app starts.  Once the app loads, everything is lickety-split.

I've seen notes and posts about the lovely withProgress() <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/withProgress.html> function. I've seen notes about how to implement when the user clicks on a tab <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/18237987/show-that-shiny-is-busy-or-loading-when-changing-tab-panels>, or when the user selects a radio button.

But how do I implement something *before* the user can click on anything?

A lot of the references I found are also a couple of years old.  Concerned about getting a "current" solution.

Any thoughts or directions are helpful.

Thanks!

-Ben

messages.subject: metaHandler Error and issue with sharing Shiny Dashboard
messages.subject_clean: metaHandler Error and issue with sharing Shiny Dashboard
messages.body_plain:
Hello there.

I'm working on a shiny app that is utilizing shinyDashboard ui commands. I noticed that when I was opening up my link, I got an error reading:

ERROR: argument "metaHandler" is missing, with no default.

The app is located on an rstudio server at my local university and a link was provided to me by a systems administrator. From what I understand, the link serves as an index to a folders that contains shiny applications.

The link can be found here:

http://rstudio.morris.umn.edu:4949/ShinyApps/ and the app I'm trying to deploy is called "small.test."

small.test is a very abridged version of the other app in the index called "test.ricky4" - which is also using shinyDashboard. Why I bring up shinyDashboard is because when I don't use shinyDasboard, I don't receive the error above.

For instance, the ui for small.test is:

> > library(shiny)
> > library(shinydashboard)
> >
> > dashboardPage(
> >   dashboardHeader(
> >     title = "CST"
> >   ),
> >
> >   dashboardSidebar(
> >     sidebarMenu(
> >       menuItem("Home", tabName = "Home"))
> >   ),
> >
> >   dashboardBody(
> >     fluidPage(
> >       mainPanel(
> >         p("It can be difficult to find population information from before 1990. Due to many requests from small communities, the Center for Small Towns is providing all population information for every county, town, and township in Minnesota dating back 1900."),
> >         p(br("This information was compiled from the U.S. Census and the American Community Survey. The following people played an enourmous role in gathering this information and developing this website."))
> >       )
> >     )
> >   )
> > )

and server is:

> > library(shiny)
> > library(shinydashboard)
> > shinyServer(function(input, output) {
> > })

and it generates the metaHandler error. Also, I'm not putting anything into the server because I'm not actually displaying any graphs or figures, I simply wanted to see if I could even display text.

Now, if I change the ui to something that isn't using shinyDashboard commands, it does not generate the error and the app shows up.

This app can be found in the folder "small.test2"

Here is the ui for small.test2:

> > shinyUI(
> >   fluidPage(
> >
> >     mainPanel(
> >       title = "CST"
> >     ),
> >     mainPanel("Home", tabName = "Home"),
> >     mainPanel(
> >         p("It can be difficult to find population information from before 1990. Due to many requests from small communities, the Center for Small Towns is providing all population information for every county, town, and township in Minnesota dating back 1900."),
> >         p(br("This information was compiled from the U.S. Census and the American Community Survey. The following people played an enourmous role in gathering this information and developing this website."))
> >       )
> >   )
> > )

and the server is the same as above.

Is there a possibility that using shinyDashboard apps can't be shared if you're not sharing your app via shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account or other alternatives?

Some assistance on this issue would be more than appreciated.

Thanks,

Ricky.

messages.subject: Using a progress bar in Shiny with rstan
messages.subject_clean: Using a progress bar in Shiny with rstan
messages.body_plain:
MCMC processing with R-packages rstan can easily keep the computer busy for several minutes, and the only feedback is the output to the console, or, when redirected, to a log file.

This is a problem when `rstan` is running in the main thread of a Shiny app, because there is no callback that can refresh the progress counter.

I have made a first attempt in implementing a progress bar with stan running in a separate process. The shiny program monitors the log file with a reactiveFileReader, updates the progress bar and displays the diagnostic plot on completion.

https://github.com/dmenne/shiny_stan_progress

This is not a package, you have to download it to your computer, and run it locally. Running it via `runGithub()` fails to display the progress bar.

messages.body_plain:
The request body is actually buffered to disk, not held in RAM, so I don't think you even really need to consider the memory limit when determining the max request size. The low default limit is mostly there to make it harder for a malicious client to fill up your hard drive (or your server's hard drive) or something like that.

messages.body_plain:
First of all, you should change your database password immediately, and in the future, don't post your password in public!

In answer to your question, you can add back all of those comment-out lines; however, the last expression in query_output needs to be the actual data (so, rs, I guess).

Like so:

query_output <- reactive({
  ...
  rs <- dbGetQuery(con, sql)
  dbDisconnect(con)
  rs
})

In this case, you should actually not do that though; instead, right after the dbConnect line, add this line:

on.exit(dbDisconnect(con), add = TRUE)

This will ensure that dbDisconnect will be called whether the reactive succeeds or fails with an error. If you don't do this but just call dbDisconnect() after dbGetQuery(), then if dbGetQuery() throws an error, the connection will not be disconnected.

It seems to work fine for me on Mac. I wonder if this is a Windows-specific issue? Perhaps sink(log_file) opens the file with an exclusive lock?

How about instead of doing sink(log_file), you use capture.output({ ... }) to grab the string output, then write it to the log file using cat(file=log_file, output)?

(BTW, I'm really hoping to have first-class support for a similar mechanism in a future version of Shiny. We want to build really good child process support into a future version of httpuv, which would make this kind of thing much easier.)

>
> I have made a first attempt in implementing a progress bar with stan running in a separate process. The shiny program monitors the log file with a reactiveFileReader, updates the progress bar and displays the diagnostic plot on completion.

messages.body_plain:
Oh, that helps. Maybe something like this (note, this is one of the only times I've ever suggested modifying a session-level non-reactive variable [ignoreNext]):

ignoreNext <- ""

observeEvent(input$sliderA, {
  if (ignoreNext == "A") {
    ignoreNext <<- ""
  }

  valB <- ...

  if (valB != input$sliderB) {
    ignoreNext <<- "B"
    updateSliderInput(session, "sliderB", value = valB)
  }
})

observeEvent(input$sliderB, {
  if (ignoreNext == "B") {
    ignoreNext <<- ""
  }

  valA <- ...

  if (valA != input$sliderA) {
    ignoreNext <<- "A"
    updateSliderInput(session, "sliderA", value = valA)
  }
})

You might also consider something like plotly, rbokeh, or dygraphs, which all have built-in zooming, or something like this <https://gallery.shinyapps.io/105-plot-interaction-zoom/> for ggplot2 (see the "Interactive Plots" section of the articles <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/> page).

messages.subject: Re: Announcing shinyFiles package
messages.subject_clean: Announcing shinyFiles package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

This is a fantastic package you got there and i'm benefit a lot from using it. I want to thank you for making this available, what an awesome package!

I do have a question relating to this package and I'm hoping that I can pick your brain.

When using Shinyfiles package, everything works well on my local machine that I am able to navigate to my local desktop to locate the file directory. However, when I deployed the application to the web on shiny server, the end user is not able to navigate to their local desktop to select the desired directory.

My understanding is that the ShinyFiles package only handle navigation of the server-side file system, so it will always show the file system of the system the app is running on (hence showing the local shiny director when it is deployed to the web).

Can you suggest a way that I can mitigate the navigation such that the end users can still navigate to their local drive using a deployed Shiny application?

Thanks!

>
> shinyFiles has now been submitted to CRAN and should hopefully be available soon.

> File sorting: Files can now be sorted by name, type, size, creation and modification date.
> Volumes: Support for multiple different roots to emulate different volumes on the file system. Furthermore a utility function getVolumes() that automatically detects the volumes available on the system.
> Responsive: The file chooser now responds to changes in the file system. Plug in a USB drive and see it appear in the list of available volumes; Delete a file on the host computer and see it disappear from the file chooser.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny R graphical design
messages.body_plain:
Best I could find is:

- Use one of bootswatch free themes ( they are recommended ? by shinyR staff, and from my experience they are pretty and generally supported - with minor workarounds- by shiny R - see the results, if you are interested dodxtx.com <http://dodxtx.com>)
 - use charts.js for graphs and charts
 - use shinyJS for button activation/ disabling and other basic java script functions initiated from server.

-  use shinyBs for tooltips, modals and collapsable

It's all free and easy to use, and looks good....

Templates like the one on forest theme may not ( or may - who knows? ) work out of box with shiny R anyways....

Best
Luke

messages.subject: dynamically expand / contract a directed graph
messages.subject_clean: dynamically expand / contract a directed graph
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have some questions about the best way to make a dynamically

expandable/contractable directed graph.  See below for specifics.

I am a newbie to visNetwork and Shiny.  I have searched various

resources and have not quite found what I am looking for.

I explain what I mean by "expandable/contractable directed graph" with

the following example:

Suppose I have a directed graphical model - a taxonomy such as the following:

-- Animal

---- Fish

---- Amphibian

---- Mammal

------ Dog

------ Cat

------ Dolphin

One way I can simply and beautifully display this with visNetwork is

as follows:

require(visNetwork, quietly = TRUE)

visNetwork(dot = 'dinetwork {"Animal" -> "Mammal" ; "Animal" ->

        "Fish"; "Animal" ->"Amphibian"; "Mammal" -> "Dog"; "Mammal" ->

        "Cat"; "Mammal" -> "Dolphin"}', width = "100%") Fish Amphibian

There are, of course, other ways to display this with visNetwork too.

Whatever.

I simply want to be able to click on a node in graph like the above

visNetwork graph and have it expand / contract (or show and hide)

dynamically.

Let me make this as clear as possible with an example:

Suppose I have the above graph displayed and I click on "Animal". At

that point the entire graph should disappear except for the node

"Animal".

Next I click on "Animal" again and the immediate outgoing neigbhoors

appear (i.e. nodes for "Fish", "Amphibian", "Mammal").

Next I click on "Mammal" and its immediate outgoing neighboors appear

(i.e. nodes for "Dog", "Cat", "Dolphin").

Next I click on "Mammal" again its immediate outgoing neighboors

disappear.

...Thats an example of what I mean by "have a graph expand and

contract dynamically" or to put it another way to "show and hide

dynamically."

KEY QUESTIONS:

(1) Is there a pre-existing code snippet / module in visNetwork and/or

Shiny someone can point out?

(2) Alternatively, do you have any guidance on how I might roll my

own?  E.g. can I / should I just do this entirely in visNetwork or am

I better off coming up to speed on Shiny as well as visNetwork.  Are

there particular functions / methods etc you recommend I look at?

Thanks very much!

Bill

messages.subject: Save plotly plots to PNG file automatically
messages.subject_clean: Save plotly plots to PNG file automatically
messages.body_plain:
I am using plotly, but would like to automatically generate an image PNG file for the same plot.

I am aware that we can call plotly_IMAGE, but this requires a call out to plotly servers which I want to avoid.

I optimistically tried putting my plot_ly call within a renderImage just to test, but it didn't work of course. Below is sample code.

Is there a way to do this please?

thanks!

ui.R

library(shiny)
library(plotly)
library(ggplot2movies)  # Needed for the 'movies' data set

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Movie Ratings!"),
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("bins", "Number of bins:", min = 1, max = 50, value = 10)
  ),
  mainPanel(
   # plotlyOutput("trendPlot"),
    imageOutput("myImage")
  )
))

server.R

Enter code here...minx <- min(movies$rating)
maxx <- max(movies$rating)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$trendPlot <- renderPlotly({
    # size of the bins depend on the input 'bins'
    size <- (maxx - minx) / input$bins

    # a simple histogram of movie ratings
    p <- plot_ly(movies, x = rating, autobinx = F, type = "histogram",
                 xbins = list(start = minx, end = maxx, size = size))

    # style the xaxis
    layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Ratings", range = c(minx, maxx), autorange = F,
                           autotick = F, tick0 = minx, dtick = size))

  })

  output$myImage <- renderImage({
    # A temp file to save the output.
    # This file will be removed later by renderImage
    outfile <- 'output.png'

    # a simple histogram of movie ratings
    size <- (maxx - minx) / input$bins
    p <- plot_ly(movies, x = rating, autobinx = F, type = "histogram",
                 xbins = list(start = minx, end = maxx, size = size))
    # style the xaxis
    layout(p, xaxis = list(title = "Ratings", range = c(minx, maxx), autorange = F,
                           autotick = F, tick0 = minx, dtick = size))

    # Return a list containing the filename
    list(src = outfile,
         contentType = 'image/png',
         width = 400,
         height = 300,
         alt = "This is alternate text")
  }, deleteFile = FALSE)

})

messages.subject: Re: Save plotly plots to PNG file automatically
messages.subject_clean: Save plotly plots to PNG file automatically
messages.body_plain:
Right. The webshot package makes this easy: https://github.com/wch/webshot

Here is a quick function that I wrote without any testing (I guess it
depends on the Github version of plotly since I'm using as.widget()
there):

#' @param x a plotly object
screenshot_plotly = function(x, file = 'webshot.png', ...) {
  file2 = normalizePath(file, mustWork = FALSE)
  d = tempfile()
  dir.create(d)
  owd = setwd(d)
  on.exit({
    setwd(owd)
    unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
  }, add = TRUE)
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(plotly::as.widget(x), 'index.html', FALSE)
  file.copy(webshot::webshot('index.html', ...), file2)
  file
}

It returns the path of a screenshot of the plotly object, which I
believe you can pass as the image path to renderImage().

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Joe! I ended up converting the jquery functions to plain javascript and removed the jquery/jquerui references (which I doubt jquery experts would agree with). Then I included the html with the great new htmlTemplate function, which was a breeze, but I still seem to be having a dependency problem. Note that originally I had built a simple ui in html as described here and everything seemed to work well. I am starting to wonder if that would be the better route. runGitHub('paulgovan/AutoDeskR') And my end goal is to make an htmlwidget out of the AutoDesk API, which I think would be really cool. Though I don't have alot of javascript experience, so I'm slowly getting there :) Thanks again, Paul On Thursday, March 10, 2016 at 7:33:14 PM UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote: > I would start by just dropping the jquery reference from your template (and if you're seeing double jqueryui references in your browser's developer tools, then try dropping jqueryui as well). I would like to create an simple app with reactive tabPanel/tabPanels which will depends on value in selectInput (I already found a solution here <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19470426/r-shiny-add-tabpanel-to-tabsetpanel-dynamicaly-with-the-use-of-renderui/19470562#19470562>). Furthermore, after I choose one value in this widget I will see different number of tabPanels which also should work as a filter. E.g. in my app I use diamonds dataset. If I choose a word 'Very Good' I will see a dataset with all rows with this value. In the top of it I will also see all unique color values in filtered dataset. What I want to achieve is to get a possibility to filter once again using tabPanels above.

library(shiny)
library(shinyTree)
library(dplyr)
library(DT)
library(ggplot2)

diamonds_test <- sample_n(diamonds, 100)
diam_cut <-
  list(
    `Very Good` = "Very Good",
    Ideal = "Ideal",
    Fair = "Fair",
    Premium = "Premium",
    Good = "Good"
  )

runApp(list(
  ui = pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel('Dynamic Tabs'),
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput('name','',choices = diam_cut)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      uiOutput('mytabs'),
      dataTableOutput('table')
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session){

    output$mytabs = renderUI({
      colorVector <- diamonds_test %>%
        filter(cut == input$name) %>%
        distinct(color) %>%
        .[['color']] %>%
        as.character()

      myTabs = lapply(colorVector, tabPanel)
      do.call(tabsetPanel, c(myTabs, type = 'pills'))
    })

    output$table <- renderDataTable({
      data <- diamonds_test %>%
        filter(cut == input$name)
      datatable(data)
    })
  }
))

messages.subject: Re: Ubuntu server runs shiny-server but shows 'application failed to start'
messages.subject_clean: Ubuntu server runs shiny-server but shows 'application failed to start'
messages.body_plain:
A couple of suggestions:

- Please check where the package is installed. You can run "installed.packages()" command in an R shell, or RStudio, and check for the location of "shiny" package. It might have been installed in a user's library instead of the site/global library.
- Depending on the version of Shiny Server you can define the following in your /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf file:

preserve_logs true;

And restart server. Then access the Welcome page again. With this setting, now the application log files will remain. You can check /var/log/shiny/server directory for the latest version of the application logs; there might be more information in the log file.

Fereshteh

I'm trying to create a dynamic label for a slider input, based on another input.  The problem is I want to use a p tag for the label with a specific class.  When I try to update the label with a p tag, the new label prints as "[object Object]", indicating a js object is getting converted to a string under the hood.   Any idea how I can fix this?

Example code:
 observe({
        newLabelText <- input$someOtherInput

        newLabel <- p(newLabelText, class = 'someClass')

        updateSliderInput(session = session, inputId = 'wantedInput', label = newLabel)
 })

messages.body_plain:
I ran into this problem today when updating to version 1.4.2 of shiny server from v1.2.3 (I think) on Mint 17.1. I followed the install instructions on the rstudio page exactly.

sudo start shiny-server worked fine before the upgrade and gives the "Unknown job" error after. What's happening is that the installer removes /etc/init/shiny-server.conf. Recreating the file with the contents in Fereshteh's reply fixes the problem. Is this an installer bug? I know Mint isn't supported, but it seems like it would be an easy fix.

Here's the output of the install command:

Preparing to unpack shiny-server-1.4.2.786-amd64.deb ...
Unpacking shiny-server (1.4.2.786) over (1.4.2.786) ...
Setting up shiny-server (1.4.2.786) ...
User shiny already exists. Ensuring proper permissions on /home/shiny/.
grep: /etc/init/shiny-server.conf: No such file or directory
Adding LANG to /etc/init.d/shiny-server, setting to en_US.UTF-8
 System start/stop links for /etc/init.d/shiny-server already exist.

On Tuesday, May 12, 2015 at 6:02:01 AM UTC-4, Jeff Parke wrote:

> Just to update - I hit the same problem on a fresh install of shiny-server on mint 17.1, and upstart won't work.
>
> /etc/init/shiny-server.conf does not exist at the end of the install. After a quick glance at the documentation, I realised /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf did exist, and copied it over. But even though they have the same name, these are two different files. shiny-server looks at /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf when starting, and this file is correctly formatted, as evidenced by the ability to start the server on the command line.
>
> Upstart looks at /etc/init/shiny-server.conf before starting it. Clearly, copying it over was the wrong thing to do, because upstart just complained it was improperly formated, it needed the fix documented above.
>
> Thanks
>
> Jeff.
>
>

> > Fereshteh

> > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 5:49:28 PM UTC-5, Raphael Nguyen wrote:
> > > Fereshteh, you're the best! This did indeed fix the error. I really hope this is the only thing that went wrong during installation as I'm worried future problems may pop up, but thank you again for all of your help. :)
> > >
> > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 2:36:31 PM UTC-8, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> > > > This is the wrong file, and it is strange that it is there.

> > > > 2- /etc/init/shiny-server.conf

> > > >
> > > > But to fix the problem, do the following:

> > > >

> > > > >

messages.body_plain:
What's the output of lsb_release --id --short from your terminal?

On Mon, Mar 14, 2016 at 10:19 AM Brett Longworth <blong...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I ran into this problem today when updating to version 1.4.2 of shiny server from v1.2.3 (I think) on Mint 17.1. I followed the install instructions on the rstudio page exactly.
>
> sudo start shiny-server worked fine before the upgrade and gives the "Unknown job" error after. What's happening is that the installer removes /etc/init/shiny-server.conf. Recreating the file with the contents in Fereshteh's reply fixes the problem. Is this an installer bug? I know Mint isn't supported, but it seems like it would be an easy fix.
>
> Here's the output of the install command:
>
> Preparing to unpack shiny-server-1.4.2.786-amd64.deb ...
> Unpacking shiny-server (1.4.2.786) over (1.4.2.786) ...
> Setting up shiny-server (1.4.2.786) ...
> User shiny already exists. Ensuring proper permissions on /home/shiny/.
> grep: /etc/init/shiny-server.conf: No such file or directory
> Adding LANG to /etc/init.d/shiny-server, setting to en_US.UTF-8
>  System start/stop links for /etc/init.d/shiny-server already exist.
>
> On Tuesday, May 12, 2015 at 6:02:01 AM UTC-4, Jeff Parke wrote:
> > Just to update - I hit the same problem on a fresh install of shiny-server on mint 17.1, and upstart won't work.
> >
> > /etc/init/shiny-server.conf does not exist at the end of the install. After a quick glance at the documentation, I realised /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf did exist, and copied it over. But even though they have the same name, these are two different files. shiny-server looks at /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf when starting, and this file is correctly formatted, as evidenced by the ability to start the server on the command line.
> >
> > Upstart looks at /etc/init/shiny-server.conf before starting it. Clearly, copying it over was the wrong thing to do, because upstart just complained it was improperly formated, it needed the fix documented above.
> >
> > Thanks
> >
> > Jeff.
> >
> >
> >
> > On Wednesday, 3 December 2014 14:55:39 UTC, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> > > Thanks Raphael. Glad that it is now working for you. And let us know if any issues pop up.
> > >
> > > Fereshteh
> > >
> > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 5:49:28 PM UTC-5, Raphael Nguyen wrote:
> > > > Fereshteh, you're the best! This did indeed fix the error. I really hope this is the only thing that went wrong during installation as I'm worried future problems may pop up, but thank you again for all of your help. :)
> > > >
> > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 2:36:31 PM UTC-8, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> > > > > This is the wrong file, and it is strange that it is there.
> > > > >
> > > > > There are 2 different shiny-server.conf files on the system after Shiny Server is installed (notice the paths):
> > > > >
> > > > > 1- /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf
> > > > > 2- /etc/init/shiny-server.conf
> > > > >
> > > > > The file you pasted is #1. If the same file also exists as #2, then something has gone wrong during installation.
> > > > >
> > > > > But to fix the problem, do the following:
> > > > >
> > > > > - Stop Shiny Server if it is running
> > > > > - sudo rm /etc/init/shiny-server.conf
> > > > > - sudo vi /etc/init/shiny-server.conf
> > > > > - Add the following lines to the file:
> > > > >
> > > > > # shiny-server.conf
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > description "Shiny application server"
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > start on runlevel [2345]
> > > > >
> > > > > stop on runlevel [016]
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > limit nofile 1000000 1000000
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > post-stop exec sleep 5
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > exec shiny-server --pidfile=/var/run/shiny-server.pid >> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2>&1
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > respawn limit 3 25
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > respawn
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > - Start Shiny Server using this command:
> > > > > sudo start shiny-server
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > Hope this fixes the problem.
> > > > >
> > > > > Fereshteh
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 4:55:42 PM UTC-5, Raphael Nguyen wrote:
> > > > > > Line 2 of that file is:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > run_as shiny;
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Here is the full file in question:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > # Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
> > > > > > run_as shiny;
> > > > > >
> > > > > > # Define a server that listens on port 3838
> > > > > > server {
> > > > > >   listen 3838;
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >   # Define a location at the base URL
> > > > > >   location / {
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >     # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
> > > > > >     site_dir /srv/shiny-server;
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >     # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
> > > > > >     log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > >     # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
> > > > > >     # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
> > > > > >     directory_index on;
> > > > > >   }
> > > > > > }
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Is it possible that the user shiny has not been created and is thus throwing the error?
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 1:52:44 PM UTC-8, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> > > > > > > What do you have as line 2 of that file?
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > You probably have something like this: env LANG='en_US.UTF-8'
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > In that case, try removing the line (or commenting it out), and retry.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 4:39:28 PM UTC-5, Raphael Nguyen wrote:
> > > > > > > > That command gave the following error:
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > ~ $ init-checkconf /etc/init/shiny-server.conf
> > > > > > > > ERROR: File /etc/init/shiny-server.conf: syntax invalid:
> > > > > > > > init:shiny-server.conf:2: Unknown stanza
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 1:36:15 PM UTC-8, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Shiny Server installation creates a job in /etc/init/shiny-server.conf. Upstart recognizes this job, and "sudo start shiny-server" command starts the job/process. But in your case Upstart doesn't recognize this job, which could be due to a syntax error (possible differences between Ubuntu and Mint). Can you try running this command:
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >  init-checkconf /etc/init/shiny-server.conf
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 3:57:10 PM UTC-5, Raphael Nguyen wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > It's alive!
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > That command worked perfectly and my Shiny Server is now up and running. I'd like to continue to troubleshoot why it wouldn't run initially if you don't mind. Does any thought cross your mind as to why it would work with this:
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > sudo /usr/bin/shiny-server --pidfile=/var/run/shiny-server.pid
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > but not with:
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > sudo start shiny-server
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > I'm afraid that not being able to run Shiny Server using the latter syntax might lead to additional problems in the future. Please share your thoughts.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 11:31:46 AM UTC-8, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > There could be some incompatibility between Upstart module on Mint and other flavors of Linux. We do not officially support Mint, but it is very possible that you could get it running. Can you try this command:
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >  sudo /usr/bin/shiny-server --pidfile=/var/run/shiny-server.pid
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > If this runs without error, then your Shiny Server has started. You can test it by accessing http://localhost:3838/sample-apps/hello/
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > Fereshteh
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 12:24:44 PM UTC-5, Raphael Nguyen wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > Hi Fereshteh,
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Following the guide, I installed r-base and r-base-dev first. Next, I installed the Shiny R package:
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny',repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > I then installed the .deb package for shiny server using:
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > sudo apt-get install gdebi-core
> > > > > > > > > > > > wget http://download3.rstudio.org/ubuntu-12.04/x86_64/shiny-server-1.2.3.368-amd64.deb <http://download3.rstudio.org/ubuntu-12.04/x86_64/shiny-server-1.2.3.368-amd64.deb>
> > > > > > > > > > > > sudo gdebi shiny-server-1.2.3.368-amd64.deb
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Running the two commands that you have listed, it seems as if both shiny-server.conf and shiny-server exists in /etc/init and /etc/init.d respectively.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > On Tuesday, December 2, 2014 9:13:48 AM UTC-8, Fereshteh Karimeddini wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > Hi Raphael,
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > Did you just install the ".deb" package?
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > Could you run the following 2 commands to see which file exists:
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > ls -al /etc/init/shiny-server.conf
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > OR
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > ls -al /etc/init.d/shiny-server
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > Fereshteh
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > On Monday, December 1, 2014 3:11:31 PM UTC-5, Raphael Nguyen wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > Hi all, I've managed to successfully install R, Shiny, and Shiny Server on my Linux Mint 17.1 box following this guide: http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/
> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > Even though the installation was successful, I am unable to use the command: sudo start shiny-server. It fails with the error message Unknown job: shiny-server. Can anyone help troubleshoot why my installation is unable to run the shiny-server command? Perhaps there are additional configuration steps that I may be missing. Please advise.
>

messages.subject: Leaflet with Shiny: reacting to input$map_zoom with leafletProxy()
messages.subject_clean: Leaflet with Shiny: reacting to input$map_zoom with leafletProxy()
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a Shiny map app using Leaflet (great package: thank you!)
I'd like my circles to increase in size as the user zooms in on the map. I have a reactive function for input$map_zoom, and use leafletProxy() to say that the circle radius should equal the zoom level. However circle radius does not change at all. Please can anyone help correct what I'm doing / identify a bug?

Reproducible example below, using an amended version of a leaflet demo from http://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/shiny.html
I've marked my amendments with a comment starting "# AC:…"

thanks in advance,
Andrew

library(shiny)

library(leaflet)

library(RColorBrewer)

ui <- bootstrapPage(

 tags$style(type = "text/css", "html, body {width:100%;height:100%}"),

 leafletOutput("map", width = "100%", height = "100%"),

 absolutePanel(top = 10, right = 10,

   sliderInput("range", "Magnitudes", min(quakes$mag), max(quakes$mag),

     value = range(quakes$mag), step = 0.1

   ),

   selectInput("colors", "Color Scheme",

     rownames(subset(brewer.pal.info, category %in% c("seq", "div")))

   ),

   checkboxInput("legend", "Show legend", TRUE)

 )

)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

 # Reactive expression for the data subsetted to what the user selected

 filteredData <- reactive({

   quakes[quakes$mag >= input$range[1] & quakes$mag <= input$range[2],]

 })

 # This reactive expression represents the palette function,

 # which changes as the user makes selections in UI.

 colorpal <- reactive({

   colorNumeric(input$colors, quakes$mag)

 })

 output$map <- renderLeaflet({

   # Use leaflet() here, and only include aspects of the map that

   # won't need to change dynamically (at least, not unless the

   # entire map is being torn down and recreated).

   leaflet(quakes) %>% addTiles() %>%

     fitBounds(~min(long), ~min(lat), ~max(long), ~max(lat))

 })

 ## AC: collects map zoom value

 mapzoom <- reactive({

   input$map_zoom

 })

  # Incremental changes to the map (in this case, replacing the

 # circles when a new color is chosen) should be performed in

 # an observer. Each independent set of things that can change

 # should be managed in its own observer.

 observe({

   pal <- colorpal()
   ## AC: circle radius set to equal map zoom

   circleRadius <- mapzoom()

   leafletProxy("map", data = filteredData()) %>%

     clearShapes() %>%
     ## AC: radius = circle radius

      addCircles(radius = circleRadius, weight = 1, color = "#777777",

       fillColor = ~pal(mag), fillOpacity = 0.7, popup = ~paste(mag)

     )

 })

 # Use a separate observer to recreate the legend as needed.

 observe({

   proxy <- leafletProxy("map", data = quakes)

   # Remove any existing legend, and only if the legend is

   # enabled, create a new one.

   proxy %>% clearControls()

   if (input$legend) {

     pal <- colorpal()

     proxy %>% addLegend(position = "bottomright",

       pal = pal, values = ~mag

     )

   }

 })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

  observe({

    req(mapzoom())
    req(filteredData())
    circleRadius <- as.numeric(mapzoom())*100
    filteredData <- filteredData()
    leafletProxy("map") %>%
      clearShapes() %>%
      addCircles(lng = filteredData$long, lat = filteredData$lat, radius = circleRadius,
                 weight = 1, color = "#777777", fillColor = pal(filteredData$mag),
                 fillOpacity = 0.7, popup = as.character(filteredData$mag)
      )
  })

If you're using custom code, then it's highly likely that the problem lies there. There are lots of things about the implementation of the Teradata drivers that might be snagging you (though I'm not very familiar with the 14.xx series so I can't necessarily help you with specifics there). Without seeing any code it's going to be absolutely impossible, though. What exactly you're doing with the JVM, either via rJava or some other method; how exactly you're managing creating and destroying connections; lots of other things - could all affect this. It could also just be a simple case of the network being faulty and dropping your connection, or the Teradata server being configured in such a way that it's dropping or refusing your connection. There is also this known issue <http://developer.teradata.com/doc/connectivity/jdbc/reference/current/jdbcug_chapter_5.html#CHDDACIH> (among many others!) with the 14.xx series of drivers, so you should definitely upgrade if you can.

This isn't about creating modules using renderUI.
With renderUI as i understand it you put a placeholder inside the UI function and then you write your controls/widget inside the server function.

Modules come in two parts. One part you have to add to the UI function and another part to the server function using callModule().

I have a slider module. I want to add it to a wellpanel when an "add" action button is clicked. If it helps you can think of duplicating the module as many times i want when a button is clicked. The duplicate modules should all be independent.

I want to know how can an action button add the UI part of the module inside the UI function and server part inside the server function.

#Dynamically adding modules
library(shiny)

#slider module ------------------------
sliderUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  sliderInput(ns("bins"), "Number of Bins:", min = 1, max = 5, value = 3)
}

slider <- function(input, output, session) {}

#shiny app ------------------------
ui <- fixedPage(
  fixedRow(
    column(width = 4, wellPanel(
      h4("Slider Module"),
      sliderUI("slider"),
      actionButton("addSliderModule", "Add Slider Module"))
    ),
    column(width = 4, wellPanel(
      h4("Dynamic Loading Modules"),
      p("Clicking on the 'Add' button on the left should add the module here. You should be able to duplicate that slider module as many times as the button is clicked"),
      hr())
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$addSliderModule, {
    #what goes here
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Each control is accompanied by an observer which stores each user setting immediately as a single key/value pair in redis. Performance and user experience ist great. You can close an app any time, open it again and continue your work at the exact state you left it. There is no noticeable delay from the redis access.

Implementation can get a bit tricky if there are complex dependencies between controls - it's difficult to control the order of the initialization in shiny.

Hope this helps

Thomas

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm not clear on what you are trying to achieve with this line ' Am[1] = renderPrint(input$num) ' .
renderPrint() is a function used to generate the required HTML output to show it on the webpage.

If you are trying to change the first cell in the matrix then you can try the below code in server.R.
Also, data read and manipulations can only be done in a reactive components inside shinyServer function.
go through this tutorial <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/reactivity-overview.html> on reactivity to understand it better.

server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output){

 Am <- reactive({
   Am<-as.matrix(read.csv("train.csv", header=F, sep=","))
   Am[1,1]<- as.numeric(input$num)
   return(Am)
 })

  output$input_coefficient <- renderTable({Am()})
})

Regards,
Sai

Sorry for not replying sooner. This is one idea:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/cedbbdde1d965fb332a5

Basically your observeEvent will help build up a list of sliderUI, and callModule(slider). And the renderUI will just display the list.

I just realized, I think you're going to find this slightly problematic at some point because adding a slider will reset all the other sliders to default values. You can fix this by changing the list of sliderUI to a list of slider id's. Then the renderUI should be modified to take the list of slider id's, and return a sliderUI with the default value set to input$duplicateSliderX if that value exists.

Sorry, this is much more difficult than it needs to be. We're talking about adding an "appendUI" type of function to Shiny itself.

chmod -R 755 /srv/shiny-server/Elections/USA2016/shiny/Temp/

messages.subject_clean: Download large csv file from a Shiny app
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am adding a download functionality to my app using downloadHandler. Everything works perfect for small dataset both locally and from Shiny server. But with large dataset (e.g. 80MB csv file), it doesn't work from Shiny server. After clicking on the download button, it takes quite a while to respond and finally shows a Server Error saying "502 - web server received an invalid response while acting as a gateway or proxy server". Anyone has any thought or experience with that? Very much appreciated.

Xiaochen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe -

Code in question: read.csv(inFile2$datapath, sep="\t", fileEncoding="UTF-16", stringsAsFactors = F)

The reason why out$assessment and output$summary are showing errors in the log (yet also showing errors in the load bar) is probably because I have an input$run condition upon loading my input csv; and I do all of my data transformation in the reactive object before it gets to output$. There are two errors I see when running the analysis on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> server:

Error: object 'bid.modifier' not found
Error: argument "subset" is missing, with no default

But I tried running this in linux environment, and I get the following message:

Warning in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines, na.strings, : invalid input found on input connection

As I mentioned before, this loads and runs fine on my local MAC.

Based on this, I'm coming to the conclusion that there may be unusual characters (i.e. ®, #, etc.) not encoded in UTF-16 csv file that breaks my read.csv code, and MACs are more robust in handling these. With that said, here are my follow up questions:
what approach do I have to avoid this situation on shiny where users are inputting their own downloaded csv with potentially unforeseen, unusual characters?
if this has more to do with what fileEncoding I'm using in read.csv, what way do I have to identify the best fileEncoding to use? I have used UTF-16 for this dataset for other cids and have worked fine so I've just assumed this is the fileEncoding for this data set.
Thanks,
Ed

You cannot blend R functions into JavaScript. str_detect() is not a
JavaScript function, so it will not work. You may google something
like "JavaScript string matching" for the correct JavaScript method.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: mmenu, work when run in rstudio but not work with shiny-server pro
messages.subject_clean: mmenu, work when run in rstudio but not work with shiny-server pro
messages.body_plain:
Wow, please ignore that reply it's flat-out wrong. I submitted a ticket with RStudio but I'll go ahead and list it here as well since it's urgent:

We are working the implement a jQuery based navigation system in Shiny (mmenu.frebsite.nl <http://mmenu.frebsite.nl>). The code is here: https://github.com/zhongxiali/mmenuShinyTest. However it does not work on a shiny server, as shown here: https://zhongxia.shinyapps.io/mmenu/. It appears that something in shinyapps.js (or shiny-server-pro.js) is overriding the capability to click on a menu to drill down to a submenu and instead it appends the selected menu to the URL.

Chris

On Thursday, March 24, 2016 at 6:02:08 PM UTC-5, hol...@geocf.com wrote:
> For those interested, it looks like mmenu relies upon a newer version of jQuery, so this fixes it:
>
> library(shiny)
> shinyUI(fluidPage(
>   suppressDependencies("jquery"),
>   tags$script(src="jquery-2.2.1.js"),
>   tags$script(src="jQuery.mmenu-master/dist/js/jquery.mmenu.all.min.js"),
>   tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "jQuery.mmenu-master/dist/css/jquery.mmenu.all.css"),
>   tags$link(rel="shortcut icon", href="favicon.ico"),
> ...
>
> On Thursday, March 17, 2016 at 12:53:50 PM UTC-5, l...@geocf.com wrote:
> > Hi,
> > I was trying to use mmenu ( http://mmenu.frebsite.nl/ ) in our shiny app.
> > I got it to work when I run it in rstudio,
> > However, it not working under shiny-server pro.
> > Does anyone have some idea on this problem?
> >
> > library(shiny)
> > library(shinyBS)
> > shinyUI(fluidPage(
> >   tags$head(
> >     includeScript(path="www/jQuery.mmenu-master/dist/js/jquery.mmenu.all.min.js"),
